thresholds.rationale: Case identity is deterministic (Phase 04): the same semantic case must always keep its case_id. Any loss breaks card history, questions and memory scope.
REV/19 acceptance: same evidence preserves cards and material changes update them. A second card for a case with a reusable card is churn management would see.
REV/19 acceptance: irrelevant changes do not trigger rewrites. Updates are patches (Phase 08): a field changes only with moved evidence and only when declared.
REV/19 acceptance: grounding thresholds are met. A committed card is the canonical output shown to management; every conclusion must trace to deterministic evidence.

Refused candidates are safe (never committed) but cost a corrective call and delay a card. More than 1 refusal in 20 answers means the prompt or model does not fit the contract; that must be fixed before release, not absorbed by re-asks.
Lifecycle is deterministic (Phase 09): a card never flip-flops within a run, never cools while its case is present, and is never shown as current while its case is absent.
Repeated processing must never ask management the same question twice or re-ask an answered one (Phase 13).
Every golden case's structural expectations describe required behaviour; one failed expectation is a failed golden case.
